Publishing on Guardian Atlas

On first use in a browser, enter the HTTPS URL of your Cloudflare authentication service. It is saved only in this browser and is intentionally absent from the public repository. Only use the service configured by the site owner.

1. Write an article

Sign in with GitHub. Open Newsletters and select an existing article or New Newsletter. Fill in the title, date, category and summary. The initial title determines the new article URL.

The Article field supports visual editing with headings, bold text, lists, links and images. Use the preview to check your content. Markdown mode is also available and can help with complex tables.

2. Add images

Upload images through the media picker. An optional cover image illustrates the article card. Compress large screenshots before uploading.

3. Save and publish

Save stores a draft on GitHub. In Workflow, review the article, move it to Ready, and select Publish. GitHub rebuilds the website; wait for Publish Guardian Atlas to finish in the repository Actions tab.

Drafts in this public repository are visible on GitHub. They are not confidential.

Edit or remove an article

Open the article and follow the same save-and-publish steps. To remove it from the list and its public URL, turn off Show on the site after publishing, then publish. Its source remains in the repository.

If the website does not update

Check that you published rather than only saved. Review the latest deployment in GitHub Actions. A failed deployment leaves the previous website online.

Add a raid video

Open Raid videos → New Video. Enter its YouTube URL, title, creator and date. Add a description and tags if useful. Save and publish as you would an article. The thumbnail and player are created automatically. Nihal’s latest uploads refresh separately at each deployment.

Update your profile

Open Contacts / About me → My profile to edit your biography, picture and contact details.
